name: 3M Grant
notes: Only teams with a 3M employee mentor may apply. US, Mexico, and Canada eligible. Submittable page currently lists no open calls (2026-27 window ended Oct 17, 2026).

name: AAUW
notes: Community Action Grants: letter of interest window closed Sept 17, 2026; decisions Nov 13, 2026; full applications by invitation only. Funds nonprofits/universities for K-12 girls STEM; AAUW branches use a separate grant. Focus on women and girls in STEM.

name: Abell Foundation
notes: Baltimore City nonprofits. Small grants (<=$10,000) reviewed on rolling basis, no deadline (first-time applicants attend info session); larger grants go to Board meetings, letter of inquiry first. Education/workforce focus; robotics not mentioned.

name: AIAA
notes: Classroom Grants up to $500/school year, paid to the school; applicant must be a K-12 teacher and AIAA Educator Associate member; aerospace-focused STEM. 2026 cycle closed. No geographic restriction stated.

name: Akamai Foundation
notes: Akamai Foundation: 501(c)(3)/public charity (or foreign equivalent) for math/science/tech education K-12; portal opens early February and closes late March annually; one request per calendar year; underserved populations prioritized. Schools not addressed.

name: American Honda Foundation
notes: A philanthropic foundation funded by American Honda Motor Co. -- a separate program from Honda's own corporate giving page (see the Honda entry).

name: Arconic Foundation
notes: In select counties only

name: Argosy New Team Grant
notes: $3,000 unrestricted for new FRC rookie teams starting 2026-27. California only. Email your Regional Director with team name, school or organization, rookie status. Deadline (extended) Oct 12, 2026; paid via Hack Club Bank.

name: AT&T
notes: By invitation only: AT&T's giving portal says funding requests are accepted by invitation only, so there is no open application. Teams usually get invited through an AT&T employee.

name: BAE Grant
notes: FIRST team grants page lists FRC, FTC and FLL application periods as closed; will prioritize teams with a BAE mentor or within 70 miles of a BAE location (per prior notes). Contact bae.firstrobotics@baesystems.com.

name: Bank of America
notes: Unsolicited applications only in posted windows (Basic Needs/Income Creation Feb 2-Mar 2, 2026; Stable Housing/Empowering Communities May 18-Jun 29, 2026); none open now. Must be 501(c)(3) (not private foundation, no fiscal agents), based in/serving eligible BofA markets. Individual K-12 schools (public/private/charter), school foundations, PTA/PTO, athletics and student trips are excluded.

name: Bausch Foundation
notes: Bausch Foundation accepts unsolicited requests on a continuing basis, reviewed quarterly; must be received two months before the Advisory Committee meeting month. Info pertains to U.S. only. Separate portals for employees and non-employees; no employee tie stated as required. No eligibility (501c3, schools) stated on the main page; no STEM/robotics focus listed (eye health, relief, community).

name: Benjamin Moore
notes: Support limited to 501(c)(3) charities in the U.S., CRA-registered charities in Canada, and HMRC-recognized UK charities; documentation of status required. Requests emailed to givingmoore@benjaminmoore.com with a 'Date Request Is Needed'. No set deadlines. Schools not mentioned.

name: BMW
notes: South Carolina only: must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) registered in SC. Rolling review (allow up to 60 days); one request per calendar year. Employee ties not required (application asks about BMW associate volunteer involvement). Excludes pro/semi-pro/recreational sports teams, political, fraternities. Schools not mentioned.

name: BNSF Railway Foundation
notes: General community grant (STEM education is a listed focus area) for 501(c)(3)s in the ~28 states BNSF operates in (Midwest, Southwest, Northwest). Contact the foundation first for asks over $10,000.

name: Boeing FIRST Grant
notes: Submittable page for the 2025-2026 form says 'no open calls'. A 2026-2027 Boeing Team Grant form exists; third-party listing shows window Aug 24-Oct 16, 2026 and that teams need a Boeing employee/retiree mentor. That 2026-2027 form reportedly lists only FLL/FTC (FRC eligibility unconfirmed). Closes earlier if funds run out.

name: Boston Scientific FRC Grant
notes: Official FIRST Submittable page shows no open calls; reported 2026 window Jul 28-Sep 30, 2026 (now closed). Within 60 miles of a Boston Scientific location in CA, IN, MA or MN (per prior notes; not on fetched page). Prioritizes economically disadvantaged schools/communities.

name: Brown Rudnick Center
notes: Underserved communities in Boston, Hartford, New York, Washington, D.C., Orange County or London

name: Canon USA
notes: Donation request form; only 501(c)(3) organizations considered; monetary or product donation at Canon's sole discretion. No dates or geography stated; schools not mentioned.

name: Cisco
notes: Applications accepted year-round via eligibility quiz, then Letter of Inquiry, then invited proposal (decisions ~1 quarter). Must be IRS 501(c)(3) public charity; program audience >65% economically underserved; sectors: crisis response, education, economic opportunity, climate resilience. Schools (public/private/charter), school foundations, booster clubs and school activities like field trips are generally ineligible. Aimed at national/multinational orgs.

name: Coca-Cola
notes: The Coca-Cola Foundation's request portal says it no longer accepts unsolicited community funding requests. Local bottlers may still handle sponsorship or product requests separately.

name: Con Edison
notes: NYC/Westchester (Con Edison service territory) only. 501(c)(3) required (educational institutions and coalitions eligible; group applications need a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent). Program support only. 2026 cycle closed; check back early 2027.

name: Costco
notes: Rolling applications (fiscal year Sep-Aug) via Benevity; 501(c)(3) only; focus on children, education, health/human services; monetary requests only; request no more than 10% of program budget; review 4-6 weeks. Page does not address schools.

name: Daniels Fund
notes: Serves CO, NM, UT, WY only. Applications by invitation/eligibility quiz, rolling basis; 501(c)(3) or government-equivalent. Schools not specifically addressed.

name: Digital Citizen Fund Rookie Team Grant
notes: For US-based rookie teams with all or majority-female membership. Up to five $5,000 grants across the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons.

name: DoDStem
notes: Must have DoD or DoDEA mentor or coach

name: Dow
notes: Dow team grant for FIRST teams with a Dow employee mentor and/or based in Dow communities (US/Canada); 2026-27 window was May 26-June 30, 2026, now closed. Dow page itself lists no application details; see FIRST team grants page.

name: Dow International Team Grant
notes: Dow FRC grant for teams outside US/Canada with a Dow mentor and/or in Dow communities worldwide. 2026-27 Submittable page says no open calls currently.

name: Dr. Scholl Foundation
notes: Letter of Inquiry window Jan 1-31, 2027 (11:59pm CT); full application due March 31, 2027 if invited. 501(c)(3) determination letter and 3 years financials required. Mostly US grants. Public schools "rarely considered"; no general support, event sponsorships.

name: Ecolab
notes: St Paul is main, other locations include: Beloit, City of Industry, CA, Clearing, IL (southwest Chicago), Elk Grove Village, IL, Ellwood City, PA, Garland, TX, Garyville, LA, Greensboro, NC, Huntington, IN, Irving / Fort Worth, TX, Jacksonville, FL, Joliet, IL, Martinsburg, WV, McDonough, GA, Naperville, IL, Sugar Land / Fresno, TX (Fort Bend County only)

name: Eversource
notes: 2026 portal closed; expected to reopen by March 2027. Must be a 501(c)(3) based in Eversource territory (CT, MA, NH). Grants typically $1,000-$10,000, rolling review 8-12 weeks, request 90 days ahead, one gift per org per year. Page lists youth robotics teams as not funded; only limited funding for school PTOs/fundraisers.

name: Fabworks
notes: Rolling sponsorship applications (no deadline) for FRC, FTC, Formula SAE, BattleBots and similar programs; accepted sponsorships last one year then must reapply; Fabworks may accept/reject at its discretion. Apply via account at fabworks.com/sponsorships. Page does not mention 501(c)(3), geography or schools.

name: Fikret Yüksel Foundation
notes: Limited to FRC teams in Türkiye (see the linked application).

name: FIRST Grant Submittables
notes: FIRST Submittable portal; currently states "There are presently no open calls for submissions." Individual grants (e.g. Rockwell) appear here when open.

name: FIRST in Texas Grant
notes: Texas only

name: FNC Bank
notes: Deadlines each year Jan 15 (March award) and Jul 15 (Sept award); next deadline Jan 15, 2027. Tax-exempt orgs (501c3) located in St. Croix, Polk or Pierce County, Wisconsin; max $2,500/yr; priority basic needs and literacy; sponsorships excluded. Schools not addressed; contact grants@fnc.bank.

name: Ford
notes: Ford Volunteer Corps / Deed employee volunteering hub (Ford work login); not a public grant application. Applicant must be a Ford employee/volunteer; no dates, 501c3, school or geography info published.

name: Ford Foundation
notes: NYC Good Neighbor Committee: applications currently closed, no upcoming deadline listed. Requires NYC-based org primarily serving five boroughs, 501(c)(3) or fiscal sponsor, focus Arts & Culture, Education, Human Services, annual budget $50K-$5M, not a current Ford Foundation grantee. Schools not addressed (community-based orgs).

name: FRC Tees
notes: Close date listed by the grantor as "TBD". Cash Credit is Restricted to Hoodies, Jerseys, and Jackets. All items are priced far lower than other services out there. More info about us at our website, and on https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frctees-2025-2026-updates-and-info/505172 contact: beckett@frctees.com

name: Gene Haas
notes: Portal opens May 1 for the following season; applications after Sept 1 are funded in January 2027 and funding ends when annual budget is used. For 26/27 priority goes to past GHF awardees; new applicants, rookie teams and teams outside US/Canada will not be awarded. Must be a public school, private school with 501(c)(3), or competition team with 501(c)(3). FRC/FTC eligible; FLL not.

name: General Dynamics NASSCO
notes: Cash contributions limited to 501(c)(3) (or 501(c)(6) for some support); copy of IRS determination required. Focus on Barrio Logan / San Diego communities served by the company. Priority for STEM education and skilled trades; employee ties give added weight but are not required. Schools are not excluded, but school trips, athletic/recreational tours and school-based sports teams are not supported. Rolling electronic form, no deadlines.

name: Glenn W Bailey Foundation
notes: Funds U.S. organizations/programs benefiting people in the U.S. (no international). Rolling monthly board review, but applications are closed for this year and expected to reopen in early 2027. One approved application per EIN per calendar year. Page does not mention FIRST Robotics or tax-status or schools explicitly; confirm with the foundation.

name: GM
notes: Available annually for sponsorship to teams with affiliated GM employees, can be a parent mentor etc. It's an internal thing so I unfortunately don't have a link to share but for anyone who works at GM and wants to know how to get sponsorship for their FRC team go to the GM FIRST Alliance Yammer page. The sponsorship covers one regional registration fee (unclear how District events are covered), and if you qualify for world's you notify them ASAP and if funds are available they'll cover the registration fee for world's.

name: Hall Family Foundation
notes: Kansas City region only (Jackson, Clay, Platte MO; Wyandotte, Johnson KS per third-party listings). Rolling inquiry form; official overview page states no eligibility details. Third-party listings say 501(c)(3), 5+ years operating, rarely operating support; education (Growing Minds) is a focus area. Unconfirmed on official page.

name: Harbor Freight
notes: U.S. only; applicant must operate locally and benefit the service area of the requesting Harbor Freight facility. Requires 501(c)(3) or (19) status held 1+ year, OR K-12 public school (NCES ID); private and post-secondary schools not eligible. One request/donation per calendar year. No published windows.

name: Honda
notes: Programmatic funding for U.S. orgs serving AL, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IN, IA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, SC, TX. 501(c)(3) (or fiscal sponsor) or NCES-listed schools/districts eligible; athletic teams and religious programs excluded. Official page showed application as closed while an Oct 1, 2026 news item says applications are open; no close date confirmed (earlier listed Oct 31, 2026), so confirm via CommunityImpact@na.honda.com. Event sponsorship closed; next window early 2027. Honda associates give no favoritism; no employee tie needed. Eligibility quiz required.

name: Idaho National Laboratory
notes: Community Development Grants go to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits; Idaho organizations get priority; individuals excluded. Annual cycle has closed in Feb in past years; current dates not found. Separate INL K-12 STEM grants (schools, Idaho) exist. Contact communityengagement@inl.gov.

name: Indiana FIRST Grants
notes: Only in Indiana. The FIRST Indiana Robotics Submittable page listed no open calls as of Nov 16, 2026.

name: Indiana Toyota Grant
notes: Only in Indiana

name: Intuitive grant
notes: Intuitive Foundation FIRST team grants (FRC/FLL/FTC) for non-rookie teams that have competed in an official event and are registered for the current season; funds paid toward registration via FIRST Finance. Portal opens June, closed Aug 14, 2026 for 2027 season; notifications October, payment November. Worldwide (US, Canada, Mexico, UK, Australia, Israel, Turkiye). No 501(c)(3) needed for US teams; no employee tie required. Schools not mentioned.

name: Investors Foundation
notes: Serves communities in New Jersey, NYC (5 boroughs) and Long Island (Investors Bank footprint). Applications via online portal; deadline not stated on the official page (third-party listings conflict: rolling vs Nov 1, 2026). Whether schools qualify is not stated; check Foundation Guidelines PDF.

name: JB Hunt
notes: Requests accepted only in December for consideration the following calendar year (via Company Giving Form); no specific dates published. Focus: health care, veterans, education, crisis management. Eligibility page not retrievable; limited funds.

name: John Deere
notes: 2026-27 FRC deadline was November 6, 2026 (review began Oct 5), though page says applications accepted while funding remains. Eligible if team is in a John Deere home community OR has a committed in-person current John Deere employee mentor/coach (retirees/dealers excluded). Covers registration, kits, field setup; not travel/event fees.

name: Johnson Controls
notes: Johnson Controls Foundation. Cycles: Dec 1, 2026 and Apr 1, 2027 (11:59pm CT). U.S.-based charitable orgs, STEM education focus; programming should serve Milwaukee WI, central PA, San Antonio TX, another US city with strong JCI presence, or have regional/national reach. K-12 schools NOT eligible. Pre-contact with philanthropy team expected.

name: Kars4Kids
notes: Rolling applications via online form; U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofits whose primary mission is serving children, secular focus; typical grant $5,000; decision in 4-6 months up to a year. Schools not mentioned; robotics not mentioned.

name: KGMIAA (Kettering)
notes: KGMIAA Robotics Grant Program for High School FIRST, VEX and RECF programs. Annual window Oct 1 - Nov 6 (year not stated); 2026 awardees listed, so currently closed. Mostly Michigan awardees; no stated geographic limit. Contact eszczepanski@kettering.edu.

name: Last Anvil
notes: Team Anvil Application: the 2026-27 cohort has already been selected. The form says the application will reopen next year.

name: Lockheed Martin
notes: Lockheed Martin does not accept unsolicited grant requests. Must be 501(c)(3) aligned with STEM workforce, Those Who Serve, or Community Resilience, located in/operating in a community where LM has employees or business interests. Public secondary schools qualify; private K-12 schools, athletic groups and individuals excluded. No employee-tie requirement stated.

name: M.J. Murdock
notes: Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, and Washington. The Trust takes Letters of Inquiry from nonprofits only during set periods; its Submittable page listed no open calls as of Nov 16, 2026.

name: Makers Making Change
notes: Canada only: Clubs That Care is for individuals aged 15-30 living in Canada (citizen/PR/refugee); needs 3 references. Applications currently closed; email info@makersmakingchange.com for next round.

name: Max and Victoria Dreyfus Foundation
notes: U.S. organizations only; must be IRS 501(c)(3) (upload determination letter, not a private foundation); will consider schools. Grants $1,000-$20,000, max 25% of 3-yr average income. Prior note says round ran May 11 - Nov 10 (dates not on guidelines page; see Timeline and Deadlines page), so presumably closed until next round.

name: McCarthey Dressman Education Foundation
notes: Academic Enrichment Grants for individual educators employed by a school or nonprofit (community center, museum) with regular contact with PreK-12 students from low-income households. Window Jan 15-Apr 15 each year or until 200 submissions; 2026 window closed. Application filed in one individual's name.

name: Meta
notes: Community Action Grants cover only communities with a Meta data center in Canada, Ireland, Denmark, Sweden and Singapore (NOT the US; US is served by the Future is for Everyone Fund). Public/state schools eligible; nonprofits use local equivalents of 501(c)(3). 2027 cycle ran Sep 14-Oct 19, 2026, now closed. Not usable by US FRC teams.

name: Michael and Susan Dell Foundation
notes: No fixed cycle or deadlines; online project submission form, foundation contacts only strong fits. Funds only focus areas and geographies (US, esp. Texas, plus India, Israel, Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Does not fund individuals, event sponsorships, or hardware/computer requests. Unlikely fit for a typical FRC team.

name: Midco
notes: Applications closed; reopen January 4, 2027. Eligible: 501(c)(3) with 509(a)(1)/(2) status, accredited schools/universities (tax-deductible gifts), or US public agencies. Midco service area (WI, MN, ND, SD, KS) gets priority but is not stated as required.

name: Motorola Solutions
notes: 2027 cycle expected to open late November 2026; close date not yet published (2026 deadline was Jan 22, 2026; estimate only). Focus: technology and engineering education and first responder programs. FAQ: employee engagement NOT required to apply but may weigh in funding; applicant must be 501(c)(3) (a secondary source says school districts also eligible); eligibility quiz first.

name: MSC
notes: Official page lists no application dates or deadlines (old "2023" form note unresolved). Requesters must be 501(c)(3), nonsectarian; no stated school eligibility or geography. Dates 2026 unconfirmed; contact MSC.

name: MSOE
notes: 2026-27 FRC/high school FTC sponsorships, $500 each. Open Sept 4; closes noon CST Dec 1, 2026; decisions Dec 4. Limited to Wisconsin and Illinois teams. Check issued to team or host organization/school. MSOE ties not required/guaranteed. FLL and middle school FTC no longer funded.

name: NASA
notes: 2027 NASA FRC grants closed Sept 30, 2026; awards posted week of Nov 9, 2026. Only Rookie / New Veteran and Year-Two (must have had 2026 NASA grant and $5,000 corporate funds) teams; no veteran grants. US-based teams only. Educational sponsor (school, 4-H, nonprofit, scouts) must submit support letter by Jan 10, 2027.

name: National Fuel
notes: Contact the Foundation representative for your state (NY, PA, OH) before applying; requests reviewed quarterly by committee, no fixed deadlines. Excludes individuals, private foundations, 509(a)(3) charities, political, amateur athletics, sectarian orgs. Schools not mentioned. Service territory NY/PA (page lists reps for NY, PA, OH).

name: NEA Foundation
notes: Student Success Grants: individual educators (teachers, ESPs, SISP) who are current NEA members in public schools or public higher ed. Fluxx registration by Nov 24; application opens Dec 1, 2026; info session Dec 15. Admins and non-members ineligible. Not available to private schools or non-school teams; applicant must be the educator.

name: Nikon
notes: US-based applicants and US programs only. Submit online at least 6 months before the program; allow 12 weeks for a response. No published open/close window. Excludes unions, political/religious causes, fundraising/raffles, individuals.

name: Nordstrom
notes: Next window Jan 1-31, 2027 (application currently closed). Funds hyper-local grassroots orgs (basic needs; economic mobility for youth/families) across the US. Excludes individual primary/secondary schools, PTOs/PTAs, athletic and religious programs, individuals.

name: Norfolk Southern Foundation
notes: 2027 Thriving Communities (sustainability, workforce development, community resiliency) and Safety First grants accept applications Feb 1-Aug 2, 2027 (5pm ET); 2026 cycle closed. In-Kind Donation grant open year-round. Covers Norfolk Southern's 22-state network. See Grant Guidelines page for 501(c)(3)/school rules.

name: Northrop Grumman
notes: All charitable grants are by invitation only; unsolicited requests are not accepted or acknowledged. Requires 501(c)(3). Focus: tech workforce access, education/work barriers, healthy sustainable communities. Non-public K-12 schools excluded; most extracurriculars excluded except STEM-focused clubs, teams and projects. No deadlines or geography listed.

name: Novelis and Ball FIRST Robotics Alliance
notes: Global FRC teams may apply; selected teams build a recycling-themed 'CanBot', collect aluminum Sept-April, post monthly on social media, check in Nov 1, bring CanBot to Worlds if qualified. Page lists no deadline and does not say if still accepting.

name: Online Metals
notes: 2026-27 sponsorship applications are open. High school and college robotics teams competing in official competitions in the US and Canada (a schools page says US high school only; confirm). No published deadline.

name: Optimum
notes: Application form (Apr 1-24, 2026 window) now shows 'This form is now closed.' Be in Optimum service areas.

name: Pershing Square Foundation
notes: Pershing Square prizes (Sohn Cancer Prize, MIND Prize, Lotus Award) fund early-career medical researchers at US academic institutions, not FRC teams; likely not relevant. Lotus Award applications open Dec 21, 2026. Existing 'Greater NYC' note is not supported by the page.

name: Pitsco
notes: Open to K-12 competitive teams (FIRST, SkillsUSA Robotics, KidWind); applications accepted each quarter (current Oct 1-Dec 31). One $450 Pitsco voucher awarded monthly, not redeemable for cash; one grant per team per 12 months. Continental US or Hawaii.

name: Polymaker
notes: Requires using only Polymaker Filament

name: PTC
notes: FRC window has closed for 2026-27; the grantor says to check back around July 2027 for the next round. FTC closed Aug 24, 2026.

name: Raytheon
notes: New nonprofit partners may apply during the open grant period June 1 - July 31 (response by December); RTX describes eligible applicants as nonprofit partners. Schools not explicitly addressed.

name: Regeneron
notes: Invitation Only (Usually means having an employee)

name: Reiman Foundation
notes: Education-focused foundation (early childhood, primary/secondary education; innovation and collaborative programs) with an online application form. No published deadlines, 501(c)(3), geography, or school eligibility on the home page; contact reimanfoundation@hexagoninc.com.

name: Rev Robotics
notes: Team REV sponsorship (FRC and FTC). FRC applications closed November 3 (Tuesday, matching 2026); FTC closed October 13. Open to US and international teams; selected teams become Team REV brand ambassadors; criteria emphasize on-field performance and FIRST community outreach. Schools not mentioned.

name: Robonauts Everybot Sustainability Grant
notes: Must be 1st or 2nd year team

name: Rockland Trust
notes: New England area (Rockland Trust footprint). Grants go to 501(c)(3) public charities in affordable housing, children and youth (not youth sports teams), financial education, small business, workforce development. 2026 grant deadline Oct 16, 2026; later applications reviewed for 2027. Event sponsorships and community donations have separate processes. Schools not addressed on page.

name: Rockwell Automation
notes: Invitation Only (Usually means having an employee)

name: Rural Technology Fund
notes: No deadlines; applications are taken year-round. $500 to $2,500 for rural technology education projects in U.S. public schools and libraries; robotics clubs and FIRST teams are named as fundable. Private and charter schools are not funded.

name: Samsung Solve For Tomorrow
notes: 2026-27 competition: applications Sep 30 to Nov 23, 2026. A STEM challenge, not a grant application: public school students in grades 6-12 enter with a teacher (21+) employed by the school, and prizes go to the school. Schools must be at least 50% publicly funded.

name: Samsung South Carolina
notes: Samsung Newberry County SC. Focus is in and around Newberry County; requests from outside South Carolina are not reviewed. Priorities: veterans, STEM education, youth. Submit via online form at least 45 days before the event. No dates, 501(c)(3) or employee requirement stated; schools not addressed.

name: SC Johnson
notes: Open to international

name: Science Education Foundation General Atomics
notes: San Diego County (countywide or multi-district impact). Funds nonprofits (EIN required); individual schools/districts only in very rare cases; school robotics clubs are not funded and are directed to the GASSSS program. Rolling 3-page proposals emailed; windows Jan-Apr, May-Aug, Sep-Dec. Awards $1,000-$10,000.

name: SCTE Foundation Grant for FIRST
notes: Requires a parent of a team member to be an SCTE (cable telecommunications engineers) member in good standing -- the SCTE-member parent submits the application. Roughly $5,000 per award historically.

name: Siemens
notes: $1,000 Siemens sponsorships for FIRST teams. Team needs a Siemens mentor, coach or family member; must download Siemens software (Solid Edge) and participate in the reference program. One application per team. Page says applications currently closed; no deadline listed.

name: Society for Science
notes: STEM Action Grants 2027 cycle: opens December 2026, deadline noon ET Feb 12, 2027; notification spring, funding May 2027. Page describes nonprofits led by social entrepreneurs; schools not explicitly addressed and 501(c)(3) not explicitly stated; confirm with grants@societyforscience.org.

name: Sony
notes: US only

name: State Farm
notes: Grants are made by invitation only each year. Unsolicited requests can be sent through a questionnaire, but State Farm says it replies only if interested, and no deadline is stated. U.S. only; eligible groups include schools and 501(c)(3) nonprofits, with K-12 STEM funding mostly near major State Farm offices.

name: Stemify Grants
notes: 1000s of grants for states and nationally

name: Swyft
notes: Team SWYFT Ambassador Program (store credit through monthly challenges, not cash). The form still shows the 2025-26 season, with FRC applications due Jan 17, 2026. No 2026-27 dates were posted as of Nov 16, 2026.

name: Target
notes: Community Engagement Funds: $1,000 to $15,000 for local 501(c)(3) nonprofits or schools (schools need an NCES number), decided by store and distribution-center leaders. Cycle 2 (Aug 3 to Sep 4, 2026) is closed; Target says to return in April 2027 for Cycle 1.

name: TD Bank
notes: Regional grants (TD Charitable Foundation) have deadlines Nov 13 2026 (passed), Mar 12, May 14, Jul 30 2027. Community Sponsorships open to for-profit and nonprofit orgs, apply 90+ days before need; 2026 sponsorship deadlines have all passed, 2027 not yet posted. Limited to TD footprint (East Coast/Mid-Atlantic/Southeast states). 501(c)(3) not stated on page; school eligibility not stated.

name: TE Connectivity
notes: Applicants must be registered nonprofit, charitable org, or educational institution (501c3 letter + W-9). FIRST application link is marked closed; Community Ambassador Program closed, 'check back in December'. FIRST grants go to teams near TE employee communities; employee affiliation must be disclosed.

name: Team Foundation
notes: Minnesota only: services must reach rural Minnesotans, preference near TEAM Industries facilities. Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or school; K-12 education is a qualifying area. No deadline published (rolling form).

name: The Standard
notes: 501(c)(3) required. Priority to orgs in Atlanta, Altavista, Cincinnati, Columbus, Dallas, Jacksonville, Minneapolis/St. Paul, Portland, White Plains (others may be considered); employee board/volunteer ties get special consideration but not required. Reviewed year-round, no deadline; Foundation gifts $5k-$25k. Schools not addressed.

name: Toshiba
notes: Toshiba America Foundation for grades 6-12 teachers; usually funds K-12 schools. Deadlines: Mar 1, Jun 1, Sep 1, Dec 1 (under $5k); May 1, Nov 1 ($5k+). Next: Dec 1, 2026. Does NOT fund club/after-school programs, summer projects, computer hardware, salaries, textbooks; one grant per school at a time; no individuals. Geography and 501c3 not stated on page.

name: Toyota
notes: Windows: May 1 (spring/summer) and Oct 1 (fall/winter); Oct 1 passed, next May 1, 2027; some facilities have own deadlines/rolling; Plano TX entities invite-only. Eligible: 501(c)(3), state/municipal orgs, public schools (private schools unaddressed). No athletic teams, member-only groups, or outside US. Must be in Toyota geographic scope (PDF on site). Employee referral name is optional.

name: Union Pacific Grant
notes: Community Ties Giving Program for 501(c)(3) public charities in communities served by Union Pacific; typical awards $5,000 to $30,000. Elementary and secondary schools can't be funded directly, though a program run in a school by a separate 501(c)(3) may be considered. The site still shows only the 2025 cycle (Apr 1 to May 14, 2025); newer dates weren't posted as of Nov 16, 2026.

name: Verizon
notes: By invitation only: Verizon says new applications are by invitation and unsolicited requests are not answered. Invited applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities or NCES-registered K-12 schools. Verizon excludes organizations with Verizon employee or family ties, so an employee connection does not help.

name: Viasat
notes: Corporate giving request form with no stated deadline. Viasat says it accepts donation requests from 501(c) charities and public or private schools.

name: W.K. Kellogg Foundation
notes: Application process is always open (letters of inquiry through the foundation's online system). Funds work on children, families, food and career pathways across the U.S., with priority places in Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico and New Orleans. Does not fund individuals or capital projects, so a robotics team is an unlikely fit.

name: Walmart
notes: Spark Good Local Grants FY27 windows: Feb 1-Apr 15, May 1-Jul 15, Aug 1-Nov 30 (page also says Dec 31 for cycle 3; confirm). Must serve the same service area as the Walmart facility requested from. Eligible: 501(c)(3), government, schools (K-12, NCES number), churches; Deed verification required. One grant per facility per org per FY.

name: Weinberg Foundation
notes: Israel, Baltimore, Northeastern Pennsylvania, NYC, San Francisco, Hawai'i (per Where We Give). 501(c)(3) or fiscal sponsor; direct services to low-income/vulnerable populations; audited financials. Education focus covers middle/high school youth programs; no colleges. No deadline stated on page; school eligibility not explicit. Unlikely fit for FRC.

name: Wells Fargo
notes: Invitation-only: invited nonprofits get a code for the online portal. Eligible: 501(c)(3), governmental agencies, tribal entities, public schools/school systems. Focus: financial opportunity, housing, small business. No deadlines or geography stated; invitation often comes via local Wells Fargo relationship.

name: Westinghouse
notes: Within 50 miles from their locations

name: Wolfspeed Grant
notes: FIRST's Submittable page listed no open calls as of Nov 16, 2026, and does not mention a current Wolfspeed cycle. Check usfirst.submittable.com directly.

name: Yawkey Foundation
notes: Eastern Massachusetts (Suffolk, Norfolk, Bristol, Plymouth, Barnstable, Middlesex, Essex) and Georgetown County SC. 501(c)(3) (fiscal sponsors OK) required; new orgs generally need $500k+ budget; eligibility quiz first. Excludes public entities incl. school districts and public/charter schools, and early/elementary programs. 2026 windows: Education Mar 2-20; Youth & Amateur Athletics Jan 2-23; Human Services Jun 1-19; Arts/Health Sep 1-18; Transformational Capital rolling. Next Education window likely March 2027.
